ai.description: *Monilesaurus montanus* is a slender lizard reaching 8–10 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and a prominent, serrated nuchal crest.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Monilesaurus montanus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, white or cream-colored spot located on the side of its neck, just above the tympanum.
ai.habitat: *Monilesaurus montanus* inhabits the high-altitude shola grasslands and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Monilesaurus montanus* is primarily diurnal, spending its active hours basking on tree trunks or rocks to regulate body temperature before foraging for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Monilesaurus montanus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Monilesaurus montanus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation montane forests above 1,000 meters.
